influences.name: Bo Diddley
influences.context: There was a Levi's commercial on the television when I was super young that had Bo Diddley doing 'Who do you Love?' while a bunch of perfect looking white kids in white shirts and 501s stood around trying to look cool but I never forgot the way that song made me feel.

influences.name: Bob Dylan
influences.context: Bob Dylan hooked me pretty damn early too.

influences.name: L. Shankar
influences.context: L. Shankar recorded a version of the Carnatic Raga Aberi with Zakir Hussain and Vikku Vinayakram and it levels me every time.

influences.name: Leonard Cohen
influences.context: An artist who has stayed with you over time? Hermann Hesse, Leonard Cohen, Van Morrison, Bob Dylan, Townes Van Zandt, Joni Mitchell, Tom Waits, Jimi Hendrix, Miles Davis, Nina Simone, Charles Bukowski and on and on…

influences.name: Mark Sandman
influences.context: I had a fake ID as a teenager and I got into a Morphine show in San Diego. They were and are one of my favourite bands of all time and I had a very illegal beer with Mark Sandman. We talked about all kinds of things but that is one of the only people I've ever felt starstruck around. A man with his own unique sound and way of writing, I was enamoured.

influences.name: Andrew Bird
influences.context: I saw Andrew Bird a few years back at Cafe Largo in Los Angeles. He's a singer/songwriter/violinist and he is out of control. Just a man with a violin, his voice, and what I'd guess is a Roland RC-20 phrase sampler pedal. Andrew is so emotive and such a great lyricist, it was terrifying.

influences.name: Lenny Bruce
influences.context: It was in LA Morrison wrote one of his most ambitious songs, the blues-flavoured TB Sheets. Its subject is the death of a young girl from tuberculosis, but it was also influenced by US comedian Lenny Bruce, who Morrison met at the club.

influences.name: Jack Kerouac
influences.context: When it comes to influences, Morrison's touchstones are as literary as they are musical. He mentions Jack Kerouac's The Dharma Bums

influences.name: Christmas Humphreys
influences.context: He mentions Jack Kerouac's The Dharma Bums, Zen Buddhism by Christmas Humphreys

influences.name: Jean-Paul Sartre
influences.context: He mentions Jack Kerouac's The Dharma Bums, Zen Buddhism by Christmas Humphreys and Jean-Paul Sartre's Nausea as being key to this work.

influences.name: Mezz Mezzrow
influences.context: Also, another really important one was Really the Blues, by Mezz Mezzrow

influences.name: Lead Belly
influences.context: My father had a lot of jazz records, and loads of blues stuff and folk stuff and, you know, Lead Belly

influences.name: Bert Berns
influences.context: when I started working with Bert Berns [the New York producer who signed Morrison in 1966], and then, you know, when I then went solo, my first solo excursion was working with him as well. But then that became restrictive. He was like an early mentor, so he opened me up to what was going on when you get into the studio, what you're trying to do in there, what the purpose is

influences.name: William Blake
influences.context: years later, when I was reading [William] Blake, I find that, ya, well, there were these experiences. I guess what Blake was writing about in his poems I connected with

influences.name: Allen Ginsberg
influences.context: I had to go back and reread Kerouac when I was, like, reading a lot of bleak material. And then there was [Allen] Ginsberg

influences.name: Seamus Heaney
influences.context: there's a Seamus Heaney book I read years ago that's called Preoccupations, and he mentions in the beginning the weather report, and that influenced me, too

influences.name: The McPeakes
influences.context: traditional Irish music wasn't really that big here except for the McPeakes. I loved the McPeakes

influences.name: Jean Cocteau
influences.context: [Jean Cocteau's] Blood of a Poet was one; it was black and white. I saw it at Queen's [University Belfast], actually. And there was another one by Cocteau

influences.name: Federico Fellini
influences.context: there were movies like this at the time, probably Fellini and some other people

influences.name: Frank Sinatra
influences.context: as Frank Sinatra said – you-have-to-take-the-blows kind of person

influences.name: Sam Cooke
influences.context: Sam Cooke was the secular version of that. Instead of being about Jesus it was about a woman, so that was soul music
